12: What to know before you start
13: FROM BASE PAY TO EMPLOYER COST THERE'S A 33% GAP, AND THAT'S THE NUMBER THAT SINKS PLANS. A Bakery Assistant at $1,490.53 a month doesn't cost $1,490.53: with payroll taxes, workers' comp and benefits on top, it costs almost $24,000 a year at full time. The La Clara team -five people, 3.5 FTEs- comes to more than $92,000 a year. That's the number you take to the financial plan.
14: THE MINIMUM WAGE IS A FLOOR, NOT A PAY SCALE. The lowest group in the example table comes to $17,886.30 a year, above the federal and Texas minimum of $15,080 a year ($7.25 × 2,080 hours). Here the minimum wage appears only as a warning: if you type a table whose lowest group falls below it, the sheet flags it. And watch your state and city: California, New York and Florida set higher minimums, and there the example table would be illegal. Check the U.S. Department of Labor's state table (updated July 1, 2026) and your city's rules.
15: THE MODEL USES 12 EQUAL PAY PERIODS. In the US there are no extra pay months, so the annual figure is the monthly figure times 12 (biweekly payroll doesn't change the annual total, only the size of each check). Overtime is a separate rule: the FLSA pays 1.5× over 40 hours worked in a week for non-exempt employees.
16: THIS WORKBOOK DOESN'T REDO JOB DESCRIPTIONS. What each role does -Head Pastry Chef, Pastry Cook, Bakery Assistant and Counter Associate- belongs with your daily task checklists, shift by shift. Here you decide how many people of each role you need, on what schedule and what they cost. They're two different questions and they don't step on each other.
17: CAMPAIGN EXTRA STAFF IS NOT BASE STAFF. Three Kings Day multiplies production kitchen output by six with the same equipment and the same people: either you bring in extra help or you don't get through it. The cost of that help is calculated below with the employer cost per hour worked, and it has to go into the cash plan for the month BEFORE the campaign, because payroll goes out before the campaign money comes in. If your extra hands are students: under 16 they can't bake, and under 18 they can't run mixers or the dough sheeter (chapter 14).
18: How often to use this workbook
19: Cadence: ONCE when you size the team, before you sign anything; AGAIN before each of the six campaigns, to decide on extra staff; and a yearly review when your state or city minimum wage changes. Day-to-day shifts aren't kept here: they're kept in the production kitchen's weekly schedule.
20: The boundary with your daily task checklists
21: Your daily task checklists have a page per role (Head Pastry Chef, Pastry Cook, Bakery Assistant and Counter Associate) with what each one does on each shift. This workbook doesn't repeat that and doesn't replace it: it builds the sizing (how many people of each role, with their pay and their payroll taxes, workers' comp and benefits) and the hiring plan with its dates. If you have both, the checklists tell you what each person does and this workbook tells you what it costs.
